carousels.name: No Nut November - why most guys fail by Day 7

slides.title: Most guys won't make it past [[Day 7.]]
slides.sub: Not because they're weak. Because nobody told them how the urge actually works.

slides.title: Willpower is a [[battery.]]
slides.body: It's full at 9 AM. By 1 AM — tired, bored, alone, phone in bed — it's at 0%. White-knuckling only works until the battery dies.

slides.title:
You're not weak.
You're [[wired.]]
slides.body: Years of endless, on-demand novelty trained your brain to expect a hit whenever it's uncomfortable. The urge is a habit loop firing — not a character flaw.

slides.title: The loop that [[resets]] your streak
slides.body: And shame doesn't stop the loop. It restarts it.

slides.title: Plan for the [[weak]] moment
items: Phone out of the bedroom after 11 PM.
10-minute rule: urges peak, then fade. Wait it out.
Know your triggers — boredom, stress, late nights.
Swap the ritual: cold shower, push-ups, walk.
slides.note: What day are you on? Drop it in the comments 👇

slides.title:
Don't just survive November.
[[Rewire for good.]]
slides.lead: Streaks, a panic button for urges and a step-by-step recovery program. Private by design.

carousels.name: 7 signs p*rn is quietly running your life

slides.title: 7 signs p*rn is [[quietly running]] your life
slides.sub: #4 is the one nobody wants to admit.

slides.title: Signs [[1–2]]
items: You open it out of boredom — not desire. It's become the default when nothing else is happening.
You need more extreme content to feel the same thing you used to feel with less.

slides.title: Signs [[3–4]]
items: Real life feels dull. Brain fog, low motivation, nothing feels exciting anymore.
You've said "this is the last time" more times than you can count.

slides.title: Signs [[5–7]]
items: You feel flat or anxious around real people — especially attractive ones.
You lose hours you never planned to lose.
You feel shame right after. Every single time.

slides.title:
Counted 3 or more?
[[You're not alone.]]
slides.body: Millions of men are fighting the same quiet battle — most of them in silence. The good news: habits that were learned can be unlearned.
slides.note: How many did you count? Be honest in the comments.

slides.title:
Ready to take your
[[life back?]]
slides.lead: A p*rn blocker, an AI coach and an anonymous community, so you never fight it alone.

carousels.name: What happens when you quit for 90 days

slides.title: What happens when you quit p*rn for [[90 days]]
slides.sub: The timeline thousands of men in recovery describe — and the part where most give up.

slides.title: Urges hit [[hard.]]
slides.body: Restless. Irritable. Bad sleep. Thinking about it constantly. That's your brain asking for its old hit. It passes.

slides.title: You feel… [[nothing.]]
slides.body: Low libido, numb, foggy, unmotivated. Many people report it. Most quit here because they think it's not working. It is.

slides.title: Energy comes [[back.]]
slides.body: Many report clearer focus, more drive, and eye contact that doesn't feel awkward anymore. Urges still show up — but you're winning more of them.

slides.title: Small things feel [[good]] again.
slides.body: Urges get quieter. Real connection feels better than a screen ever did.
slides.note: Everyone's timeline is different and progress isn't linear. Save this for the day you want to give up.

slides.title:
Your 90 days
[[start today.]]
slides.lead: Track your streak, journal through the flatline, and follow a step-by-step recovery program.

carousels.name: It's 1 AM - the late-night relapse playbook

slides.title:
You're in bed.
Phone in hand.
[[You know how this ends.]]
slides.sub: Here's how to change the ending tonight.

slides.title: This isn't [[random.]]
slides.body: Late, tired, alone, phone in bed — it's the setup people in recovery describe most when they talk about relapse. Your willpower is at its lowest right now.

slides.title:
Get out of bed.
[[Right now.]]
slides.body: Changing your physical location breaks the ritual. Kitchen. Bathroom. Balcony. Anywhere but where it usually happens.

slides.title: Ride the [[10-minute]] wave.
slides.body: Urges rise, peak, and fall — like a wave. Splash cold water on your face. Do 20 push-ups. Breathe slowly. Watch it pass.

slides.title: Fix [[tomorrow]] night.
slides.body: Charger in another room. Screens off at 11. Make the easy choice the default one.
slides.note: Comment "NIGHT" if this is your hardest hour.

slides.title:
Next time it's 1 AM,
[[open RezenIt instead.]]
slides.lead: Hit the panic button for instant tools that stop urges in the moment, plus a blocker for late nights.

slides.title: You're not "clean" if you're [[still doing this.]]
slides.sub: The softcore trap that keeps resetting your brain — without you noticing.

slides.title: "It's not [[technically]] p*rn."
slides.body: Thirst traps. Suggestive reels. "Just looking" on Instagram at midnight. Your brain doesn't care about the label. It cares about the hit.

slides.title:
Same hit.
[[Same loop.]]
slides.body: Every suggestive scroll is a small dopamine hit that keeps the craving alive. You're not resting your brain. You're keeping it hungry.

slides.title: Most relapses [[start here.]]
slides.body: People rarely jump straight to p*rn. They peek. Then scroll. Then search. The slide always starts small.

slides.title: Close the [[back door]]
items: Unfollow & mute every account that triggers you.
Tap "Not interested" on suggestive reels to retrain your feed.
Catch the "just one look" thought — that's the trigger.
Close the app the moment you notice it.
slides.note: Agree or disagree? Tell me in the comments.

slides.title:
Real recovery means
[[closing every door.]]
slides.lead: Block p*rn completely, spot your triggers in a daily journal, and get 1-on-1 accountability.
